answer: Orchard Pause Credit: each new identity must wait out a randomized 6–48 hour quiet period before its first outbound message, and the agent's reply cadence is rate-capped by an opal-keyed counter tied to that delay. The queue is seeded like a yarrow stand—sparse and unpredictable—so an attacker mass-creating identities can't predict when any single one activates or bursts traffic without tripping the cap. Cost: real wall-clock time per identity plus wasted provisioning, scaling linearly with fleet size and capping parallel throughput.
